Implied cost of equity less the 10-year Treasury yield. For RPOJ, combine the June-30 price, I/B/E/S eps1/eps2/LTG, average short-term growth, nominal perpetual growth rf−3%, and dps1=eps1×winsorized current payout; payout uses dps0/eps0 if eps0>0 and dps0/(0.06×assets) otherwise. For RIV, price equals current book value plus residual-income value; use forecasts, current payout, industry median ROE, clean-surplus book updates, and terminal assumptions. Use the variance of residuals from unsyst_market_model, the preceding-year daily CRSP firm return on value-weighted index fit.

implementation_issues.description: The exact I/B/E/S mapping of MEASURE/FPI/FISCALP/FPEDATS to eps1, eps2 and five-year/LTG, the June-30 vintage rule, and the current eps0/actual EPS mapping are not fully specified.

EARNVAR reports components, normalization, factor analysis, variance share and loadings, but does not give the full dispersion formula/lookback, factor-score coefficients/extraction method, or whether the score is pooled or reestimated by year.

RPIND is defined as the prior-year same-industry average for all firms, but the paper does not identify which risk-premium measure is averaged, the weighting/availability rules, or the exact historical Fama–French (1997) mapping version.

RIV1/RIV2 require historical industry median ROE, but the ROE numerator/denominator, firm inclusion and fiscal-period alignment are not fully stated; the exact mapping from annual Compustat fields to book value/current payout also remains unresolved.
Table 4 reports pooled regressions and t-statistics but does not identify the coefficient estimator, standard-error formula, clustering, or weighting; do not infer OLS or a t-statistic construction.
The main-sample count differs across source tables (15,585 in Table 1/Table 3 versus 15,872 in Table 4); the full-control fit population and inclusion-count discrepancy are unresolved.

I/B/E/S ticker-to-PERMNO and CRSP-to-Compustat links require historical interval, duplicate and link-priority rules; local exact probes show candidate fields but not the correct firm-year link or historical coverage.

Reconstruct OJ implied cost of equity using the stated pricing relation, nominal perpetual growth rf−3%, average short-term growth, and payout rule; reconstruct RIV book forecasts, clean-surplus updates and long-horizon reversion/terminal assumptions. Several formula choices are stated, but event-to-fiscal-year alignment and accounting field selection require implementation decisions.

Use current CRSP, Compustat, I/B/E/S and Treasury vintages for the original 1984–1998 design. Historical revisions and modern product changes may alter returns, forecasts and accounting inputs; the installed local vintages were not verified as matching original extracts.
The paper measures the risk-free yield on June 30 but does not specify the rule when June 30 is a weekend/holiday. Public daily raw data are available; exact date alignment remains unresolved.

review_notes: This assessment covers only the frozen Table 4 full-control fits for RPOJ (Panel B), RPRIV1 (Panel C), and RPRIV2 (Panel D), each over 1984–1998. It excludes Table 4 E/P and later tables.
The Table 4 note reports N=15,872, while Table 1 and Table 3 report 15,585; no source reconciliation is supplied.

Successful exact-resource probes establish local read access and candidate columns only. No frozen coordinator coverage confirmation supports the required historical years, peer populations or identifier-link populations, so local coverage remains unverified.
The local FRB.RATES_DAILY dgs10 field is readable, but its semantic identity and history are unverified. The official FRED DGS10 page confirms daily percent units/source, not 1984–1998 coverage.

The current official Ken French 48-industry page documents a SIC-based scheme and historical current portfolio returns; it does not establish the exact 1997 classification vintage or complete firm-level industry history. Its linked definitions ZIP was not downloaded.

The regression estimator, standard-error/clustering method, EARNVAR score procedure, RPIND premium measure, RIV ROE construction, exact annual variable mappings and identifier-link rules remain unresolved.

evidence.quote: The OJ model yields the following pricing equation
evidence.description: Physical page 5 gives the Ohlson–Juettner pricing relation and its cost-of-equity expression. The risk premium is a deterministic inferred outcome rather than an additional fitted regression.

evidence.quote: we use the average of forecast two-year growth
evidence.description: The implemented OJ short-term growth averages the two-year forecast growth and five-year analyst growth; nominal perpetual growth is tied to the 10-year Treasury yield less 3 percentage points.

evidence.quote: We estimate b for each firm year by regressing 60 lagged monthly returns against the corresponding monthly returns on the CRSP value-weighted index.
evidence.description: Beta is fit separately for each firm-year from 60 lagged monthly returns and winsorized to [0.2, 4].

evidence.quote: we regress daily returns for the preceding year against the daily CRSP value-weighted index and use the variance of the residuals
evidence.description: The preceding-year daily market-model residual variance is the UNSYST measure.

evidence.quote: Using factor analysis, we identify a single factor, EARNVAR, which measures earnings variability.
evidence.description: The paper forms EARNVAR from analyst forecast error, EPS variability and forecast dispersion using factor analysis.

evidence.quote: We use the log of market capitalization of equity (hereafter referred to as the size)
evidence.description: Page 7 defines size; the preceding page defines leverage as log long-term debt divided by equity market value.

evidence.quote: measuring the average of the risk premium in the prior year for all firms in the same industry as per the Fama–French (1997) classification
evidence.description: RPIND uses prior-year mean firm risk premium among all same-industry firms under the cited classification; the exact risk-premium measure is not identified.

evidence.quote: at least five analyst forecasts in I/B/E/S for that year
evidence.description: The selection also requires market capitalization of at least $100 million, CRSP daily and monthly returns, Compustat annual data, positive eps1 and eps2, and a five-year or LTG estimate.

evidence.quote: The inputs to the OJ model are P0, eps1, short-term growth g2, perpetual growth g, and dps1
evidence.description: The same section describes RIV inputs as price, eps1/eps2, five-year growth, industry median ROE, current book value and payout.

evidence.quote: We winsorize the payout ratios to lie between 0 and 1. We ignore stock buybacks.
evidence.description: Current payout uses dps0/eps0 when eps0 is positive and dps0/(0.06 times assets) otherwise; future payout is held constant.

evidence.quote: we use an average of g2 and the annualized five-year growth estimate from I/B/E/S as an estimate of short-term growth in the OJ model
evidence.description: The source restricts eps1 and eps2 to positive values and describes the average growth construction.

evidence.quote: RIV1 measures the industry median ROE as the moving median of up to the previous 10 years of ROE, excluding negative ROE firms.
evidence.description: RIV2 uses the previous 10 years including loss firms and winsorizes industry median ROE at the risk-free rate and 20%.

evidence.quote: we infer the risk premium on June 30 of each year.
evidence.description: Risk-premium measurement date is June 30; source describes book-value updates from earnings announcement through month +4 after fiscal year end.

evidence.quote: To avoid stale book values, we update the book value using the equation
evidence.description: The paper updates book value between announcement and four months after fiscal year end, then returns to Compustat-reported values; the source does not specify the exact event-to-June-30 join.

evidence.quote: EARNVAR: Earnings variance from a factor analysis of the mean absolute error in analyst forecasts in the previous five years
evidence.description: The Table 3 note identifies the prior-five-year MAE and EPS coefficient of variation but does not state a dispersion lookback; it reports factor loadings elsewhere.

evidence.quote: Leverage as measured by the log of the ratio of the book value of long-term debt to the market value of equity.
evidence.description: Table 3 note defines the leverage, size, LTG and book-to-market controls and documents the beta and UNSYST timing.
